1 جَرَنَ , (S, K,) aor.
جَرُنَ , (S,) inf. n. جُرُونٌ, (S, K,) said of a man, and of a beast, (ISk, S,) He became accustomed, habituated, or inured, to a thing, or an affair. (ISk, S, K.) And جَرَنَتْ يَدَاهُ عَلَى العَمَلِ, inf. n. as above, His hands became accustomed, or inured, to the work. (M, TA.) ―
-b2- Also, said of a garment, or piece of cloth, (S, K,) and of a coat of mail, (K,) and of a skin for water or milk, (S,) It became threadbare, or worn, and soft, or smooth: (S, K:) or, said of a skin, and of a book, or writing, it became old and worn out. (M, TA.) ＝
-A2- جَرَنَ, (K,) inf. n. جَرْنٌ, (TA,) He ground grain (K, TA) vehemently: (TA:) of the dial. of Hudheyl. (TA.)
From An Arabic-English Lexicon (Edward William Lane)
